title: LegalEvolver: Agentic Legal Judgment Prediction via Rubric-Guided Self-Evolution
title_zh: LegalEvolver：基于评分标准引导的自进化智能体法律判决预测

paragraphs.en: As LLM-based agents develop, they have been increasingly applied in the legal domain. Legal Judgment Prediction (LJP) requires models to conduct multi-step reasoning and external legal evidence retrieval. Existing legal search agents’ performance is often constrained by the quality of retrieval queries. They often formulate queries directly from the initial user request, overlooking latent legal issues and legally salient details. To address this issue, we propose LegalEvolver , a query optimization framework specifically designed to generate legally informative queries for LJP-oriented retrieval. Sampling high-quality optimized queries and their corresponding search trajectories is challenging, as relying solely on unguided high-temperature rollouts is both inefficient and constrained by the model’s initial capabilities. We therefore heuristically optimize queries as seeds, improving the efficiency of trajectory generation. Furthermore, we summarize rollout experience into rubrics and use them to guide multi-round iterative self-evolution. Iteratively performing rubric optimization and rubric-guided RL enables the model to surpass its initial performance ceiling. End-to-end performance on extensive benchmarks demonstrates the effectiveness of query optimization on LJP. Comparisons with direct SFT followed by RL demonstrate the effectiveness of rubric guidance. Evolving rubrics further outperform fixed rubrics, confirming the benefits of self-evolution.

paragraphs.en: Legal judgment prediction (LJP) requires a model to determine the applicable law articles, charges, and prison term of a case from its fact description ( Xu et al., 2020 ) . Like a judge, the model must establish the charge before determining the sentence ( Zhong et al., 2018 ) . Decisions must be based on specific legal provisions, which come from statutes, judicial interpretations, and sentencing guidelines ( Wu et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) . Because these provisions are numerous and frequently revised, parametric knowledge alone cannot capture them reliably ( Deng et al., 2024a ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . Therefore, recent work turns to legal search agents, which consult these sources along with precedents during reasoning and base their predictions on the retrieved evidence ( Wu et al., 2023 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 法律判决预测（LJP）要求模型根据案件的事实描述确定适用的法条、罪名和刑期（Xu et al., 2020）。 与法官一样，模型必须先确定罪名，再进行量刑（Zhong et al., 2018）。 判决必须依据具体的法律规定，这些规定来自成文法、司法解释和量刑指南（Wu et al., 2023；Wang et al., 2024）。 由于这些规定数量众多且频繁修订，仅靠参数化知识无法可靠地掌握它们（Deng et al., 2024a；Yang et al., 2026）。 因此，最近的工作转向法律搜索智能体，这类智能体在推理过程中查阅这些来源以及先例，并基于检索到的证据做出预测（Wu et al., 2023）。

paragraphs.en: However, access to retrieval alone brings modest gains ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . Our analysis shows that queries themselves are often the problem of failure; this diagnosis is consistent with recent work on query optimization for search agents ( Li et al., 2025b ; Wen et al., 2026 ) . Consider a defendant who borrows the victim’s phone and then runs off with it. The query “elements of the crime of fraud” fails because the key point is the victim’s intent in handing over the phone, which is exactly what separates fraud from theft. A better query is like “took a borrowed phone and fled, whether the victim disposed of property, theft versus fraud”. To understand what distinguishes effective queries more generally, we examine the reasoning and search trajectories of legal experts on judgment prediction. Experts rarely search for a charge or an article in isolation. Each query addresses a question still open at that point of their reasoning, and changes as the reasoning moved on. When deciding the charge, they search statutes and judicial interpretations; when deciding the sentence, they searched sentencing guidelines and precedents. In both stages, they wrote the decisive facts of the case into the query ( Wen et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 然而，仅拥有检索访问能力带来的提升有限 ( Wang et al., 2024 ) 。 我们的分析表明，查询本身往往就是失败的问题所在；这一诊断与近期关于搜索智能体查询优化的工作一致 ( Li et al., 2025b ; Wen et al., 2026 ) 。 设想一名被告人借用了受害者的手机，然后拿着手机跑掉了。 查询「诈骗罪的构成要件」之所以失败，是因为关键在于受害者交出手机时的意图，而这正是区分诈骗与盗窃的关键。 更好的查询类似于「拿走借来的手机并逃离，受害者是否处分了财产，盗窃与诈骗之辨」。 为了更普遍地理解什么样的查询才有效，我们考察了法律专家在判决预测任务中的推理与检索轨迹。 专家很少孤立地检索某个罪名或某条法条。 每个查询都针对其推理过程中某一时刻尚未解决的问题，并随着推理的推进而变化。 在决定罪名时，他们检索法条与司法解释；在决定量刑时，他们检索量刑指南与先例。 在这两个阶段中，他们都会把案件的决定性事实写入查询 ( Wen et al., 2026 ) 。

paragraphs.en: Search agents are commonly trained with SFT followed by RL with outcome rewards ( Li et al., 2025a ) . This recipe struggles to inject the behaviour described above for the following reasons ( Chu et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) : (1) Exploration stays anchored to the model’s initial hypothesis ( Chu et al., 2025 ) . Once the base model settles on a candidate charge, its queries keep revolving around it. Higher sampling temperature hardly varies charge under examination ( Chen et al., 2025 ) . (2) Outcome rewards cannot tell which search went wrong ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . It fails to distinguish different search failure types ( Li et al., 2025b ) . General query clarity and informativeness also miss these domain-specific legal requirements ( Deng et al., 2024a ; Liu et al., 2026 ) . (3) What makes a query useful changes as the agent improves ( Shao et al., 2025 ; Gunjal et al., 2025 ) . Once the agent routinely includes key facts, its remaining errors can depend on subtler distinctions ( Xu et al., 2020 ) . Fixed criteria fail to separate good queries from bad ones ( Shao et al., 2025 ) .

paragraphs.en: The key missing ingredient is supervision for individual queries. Our core observation is that differences in judgment outcomes can provide it. When trajectories on the same case reach different judgments, the differences between their queries suggest which searches are more effective. The type of error further indicates which searches to examine. A wrong charge points to the searches for legal qualification, while a wrong sentence points to the sentencing searches. Building on this observation, we induce query criteria from within-case contrasts and assemble them into rubrics that reward each search. As the policy improves, we rebuild the rubrics from its new trajectories. The supervision thus evolves with the policy.
paragraphs.zh: 关键的缺失要素是对单个查询的监督。 我们的核心观察是，判断结果的差异可以提供这种监督。 当同一案件的多条轨迹得出不同的判断时，它们查询之间的差异表明哪些搜索更有效。 错误的类型进一步指出了应当检查哪些搜索。 错误的罪名指向法律定性相关的搜索，而错误的量刑指向量刑相关的搜索。 基于这一观察，我们从案例内对比中归纳查询标准，并将它们组装成对每次搜索进行奖励的量规。 随着策略的改进，我们根据其新轨迹重建量规。 因此，监督随策略一同演进。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we propose LegalEvolver, a framework for training legal search agents. It learns query rubrics from the agent’s own trajectories and keeps refreshing them as the agent improves. Training consists of three consecutive stages. (1) Diverse Trajectory Generation and Policy Initialization. We first sample diverse reasoning and retrieval trajectories at a high temperature, then apply expert-inspired heuristics to rewrite their retrieval queries, producing additional candidate trajectories. Rejection sampling selects successful trajectories for supervised fine-tuning, equipping the agent with effective initial reasoning and retrieval behaviors. (2) Initial Rubric Construction. To construct query-level supervision, we contrast successful trajectories with failed trajectories for the same problem, examining how differences in query construction contribute to their divergent outcomes. We distill these comparisons into an initial set of legal query rubrics that provide explicit criteria for evaluating intermediate queries. (3) Rubric–Policy Co-Evolution. Building on this initialization, we jointly improve the query rubrics and the agent policy through iterative self-evolution. We combine rubric-based rewards with outcome rewards for reinforcement learning, providing feedback on both intermediate query quality and final prediction correctness. As the updated policy generates new successful trajectories, we use them to re-induce the rubrics, incorporating retrieval strategies discovered during training. The revised rubrics then guide the next round of policy optimization. Alternating these steps lets supervision evolve with the agent’s capabilities, enabling improvement beyond the initial demonstrations and fixed rubric criteria.

paragraphs.en: Experiments on single- and multi-defendant legal judgment prediction show that LegalEvolver outperforms agentic retrieval-augmented baselines on most metrics, with further gains from reinforcement learning after supervised initialization.

paragraphs.en: Legal Judgment Prediction (LJP) has been studied using neural classification models ( Zhong et al., 2018 ) , LLM-based legal reasoning ( Jiang and Yang, 2023 ) , and agents that acquire external legal knowledge ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . Early work models dependencies among judgment subtasks with TopJudge ( Zhong et al., 2018 ) , distinguishes confusing law articles with LADAN ( Xu et al., 2020 ) , and incorporates case circumstances with NeurJudge ( Yue et al., 2021 ) . With the emergence of LLMs, legal syllogism prompting and syllogistic judgment analysis explicitly structure legal reasoning ( Jiang and Yang, 2023 ; Deng et al., 2023 ) . ADAPT further employs an Ask–Discriminate–Predict framework to distinguish confusing charges ( Deng et al., 2024b ) . External knowledge also supports judgment prediction through precedent-enhanced LLM and domain-model collaboration ( Wu et al., 2023 ) and multi-stage knowledge integration ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . GLARE expands confusing charge candidates and retrieves reasoning paths from similar cases for comparative reasoning ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . Query formulation is itself relevant to legal retrieval: knowledge-guided case reformulation has been studied for interpretable case matching ( Deng et al., 2024a ) . We focus on learning to formulate intermediate retrieval queries within an LJP agent, using case facts to seek the legal knowledge needed for judgment reasoning.

paragraphs.en: Rubric-based supervision expresses response quality through explicit criteria, supporting both model evaluation ( Liu et al., 2023 ) and policy optimization ( Gunjal et al., 2025 ) . G-Eval combines specified evaluation criteria with generated evaluation steps and structured scoring ( Liu et al., 2023 ) . AutoCalibrate induces scoring criteria from human-labeled examples, then selects and refines them to improve agreement with human judgments ( Liu et al., 2024 ) . For contrastive construction, OpenRubrics derives explicit constraints and implicit quality principles by comparing preferred and rejected responses, producing criteria that distinguish their quality ( Liu et al., 2026 ) . Rubrics as Rewards aggregates instance-specific rubric feedback into rewards for on-policy RL beyond verifiable domains ( Gunjal et al., 2025 ) . DR Tulu further maintains evolving rubrics that adapt with the policy to provide discriminative feedback during deep-research training ( Shao et al., 2025 ) . These works motivate preference-based criterion induction ( Liu et al., 2026 ) and adaptive rubric supervision ( Shao et al., 2025 ) . We extend these ideas to tool-specific legal queries: downstream judgment outcomes determine trajectory preferences, from which we discover and refine rubrics for supervising intermediate retrieval actions. An extended discussion of reinforcement learning for tool-using and search agents is provided in Appendix A .

paragraphs.en: We adopt the ReAct framework ( Yao et al., 2023 ) as the backbone of our legal search agent. The legal agent performs multi-round interactions with external legal retrieval tools through a sequence of Reasoning–Action–Observation steps. We represent the reasoning process of the legal agent as a trajectory: τ = ( f , r 1 , a 1 , o 1 , … , r m , a m , o m , y ^ ) \tau=(f,r_{1},a_{1},o_{1},\ldots,r_{m},a_{m},o_{m},\hat{y}) , where r j r_{j} denotes the natural-language legal reasoning at step j j , a j a_{j} represents the tool-use action taken by the agent, o j o_{j} denotes the corresponding retrieval observation returned by the tool, and y ^ \hat{y} represents the final prediction generated by the agent. y ^ \hat{y} consists of predicted law articles l ^ \hat{l} , predicted charges c ^ \hat{c} , and the predicted term of imprisonment t ^ \hat{t} . For a retrieval action, the agent can send a query to one of the four legal knowledge bases: law articles, precedents, judicial interpretations, and sentencing guidelines. Appendix C describes these knowledge sources and their retrieval interfaces.

paragraphs.en: For each training case, we sample multiple trajectories at an elevated temperature to explore different reasoning paths and queries. Our preliminary study identifies poorly constructed queries as the main failure source, as detailed in Section 4.3 . We analyze the failed search trajectories and group their recurring query failures into three patterns: (1) Queries often consist only of a charge name, generic legal terms, or a specific article number, leaving the underlying legal question implicit; (2) Queries may omit facts needed to distinguish charges or determine a sentencing range, even when the general retrieval intent is clear; (3) Searches may remain anchored to an incorrect charge or article, conflate multiple charges, or repeat an early hypothesis without using retrieved evidence to seek new discriminating information.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个训练案例，我们以较高的温度采样多条轨迹，以探索不同的推理路径和查询。 我们的初步研究发现，构建不佳的查询是主要的失败来源，详见第 4.3 节。 我们分析了失败的搜索轨迹，并将其反复出现的查询失败归为三种模式：(1) 查询往往仅包含罪名、泛化的法律术语或某个具体条文编号，使背后的法律问题隐而不显；(2) 即使总体检索意图清晰，查询也可能遗漏区分罪名或确定量刑区间所需的事实；(3) 搜索可能始终锚定在错误的罪名或条文上、混淆多个罪名，或在未利用检索到的证据来寻找新的区分性信息的情况下重复早期假设。

paragraphs.en: Comparing these patterns with human experts’ LJP trajectories motivates three complementary rewriting strategies: (1) Conservative rewriting. Human experts formulate explicit questions around the legal uncertainty they need to resolve. We therefore clarify the intended legal issue and make the query more specific while preserving its original information need. (2) Fact-enriched rewriting. Human experts ground their searches in legally decisive case details. We therefore enrich queries with relevant facts from the case description, including conduct, consequences, and circumstances. (3) Targeted repair rewriting. Human experts adapt their searches to unresolved issues and prior findings. We therefore use the trajectory’s outcome state ( S 1 S_{1} or S 2 S_{2} ), the retrieval tool, and the search history to revise the search direction: legal qualification failures ( S 1 S_{1} ) motivate queries about statutory elements and distinctions between candidate charges, whereas sentencing failures ( S 2 S_{2} ) motivate queries about sentencing thresholds and adjustment factors. Prior queries and results guide which unresolved issue to investigate next.
paragraphs.zh: 将这些模式与人类专家的 LJP 轨迹进行比较，可以启发三种互补的重写策略：(1) 保守式重写。 人类专家会围绕他们需要解决的法律不确定性提出明确的问题。 因此，我们在保留原始信息需求的同时，澄清预期的法律问题并使查询更加具体。 (2) 事实增强式重写。 人类专家会依据法律上起决定作用的案件细节来开展检索。 因此，我们用案件描述中的相关事实来丰富查询，包括行为、后果和情节。 (3) 针对性修复式重写。 人类专家会根据未解决的问题和先前的发现来调整他们的检索。 因此，我们利用轨迹的结果状态（S 1 S_{1} 或 S 2 S_{2}）、检索工具和搜索历史来修正搜索方向：法律定性失败（S 1 S_{1}）会促使生成关于法定构成要件以及候选罪名之间区别的查询，而量刑失败（S 2 S_{2}）则会促使生成关于量刑门槛和量刑调节因素的查询。 先前的查询和结果会指引下一步应当调查哪个未解决的问题。

paragraphs.en: Using the outcome states and preference ordering defined in Section 3.1 , we construct three types of within-case preference pairs: S 3 S_{3} versus S 2 S_{2} , S 2 S_{2} versus S 1 S_{1} , and S 3 S_{3} versus S 1 S_{1} , with the first trajectory preferred in each pair. These pairs provide the input to pairwise criterion discovery. These pairs are sampled from the initial trajectory pool P 0 P_{0} . Each pair of trajectories comes from the same case. Since we have four legal retrieval bases, the legal search agent has access to 4 retrieval tools. As for the outcome dimension, we define three reasoning focuses: Sentencing ( S 3 S_{3} versus S 2 S_{2} ), Legal Qualification ( S 2 S_{2} versus S 1 S_{1} ), and Full Repair ( S 3 S_{3} versus S 1 S_{1} ). Thus, we organize criteria into 12 (4 × \times 3) tool-focus groups, each forming a rubric with multiple criteria. Let 𝒰 \mathcal{U} denote the set of four retrieval tools and ℱ \mathcal{F} the set of three reasoning focuses. paragraphs.en: We construct the initial rubric bank ℛ 0 \mathcal{R}_{0} in three steps. (1) Pairwise Criterion Discovery. We use a strong LLM to compare the preferred and rejected trajectories in the context of the case and interaction history. It identifies differences in query content and search focus, then proposes criteria for the corresponding tool-focus group. Each candidate includes a description, a four-level scoring guide, and a confidence score. (2) Criteria Aggregation. Within each group, we remove incomplete, ambiguous, and low-confidence candidates. Then we merge duplicates and cluster related criteria into reusable guidance. For each group, criteria aggregation combines evidence across pairs into a candidate rubric. (3) Criteria Validation. We test the aggregated criteria on held-out trajectory pairs and retain those that consistently assign higher scores to preferred-side queries across sufficient examples. paragraphs.en: Typical agent training involves SFT followed by RL ( Cai et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) . To enable the agent to surpass the capability ceiling of this training paradigm, we propose a rubric-based co-evolutionary self-improvement paradigm in which the policy and rubric bank improve through alternating updates. Here k k indexes co-evolution rounds, and ℛ k ​ ( u , F ) \mathcal{R}_{k}(u,F) denotes the rubric associated with tool u u and focus F F in the round- k k bank. paragraphs.en: We compare our method against four categories of baseline approaches. (1) Classification Methods: We consider four supervised classification methods for LJP, including TopJudge ( Zhong et al., 2018 ) , NeurJudge ( Yue et al., 2021 ) , BERT ( Devlin et al., 2019 ) , and LawFormer ( Xiao et al., 2021 ) . (2) Direct Reasoning: We use a range of models to predict judgments directly from case facts without external retrieval, including Qwen3-8B ( Qwen Team, 2025 ) , GLM-4-9B ( Zeng and others, 2024 ) , Hunyuan-A13B ( Team et al., 2026 ) , Qwen3-14B ( Qwen Team, 2025 ) , GLM-4-32B ( Zeng and others, 2024 ) , and Qwen-Max ( Bai and others, 2023 ) . (3) Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning: Agentic RAG combines multi-step reasoning with external legal evidence retrieval. Search-o1 interleaves reasoning and search to acquire supporting evidence ( Li et al., 2025b ) . PLJP uses domain models to generate candidate labels and retrieve precedents for LLM prediction ( Wu et al., 2023 ) . GLARE distinguishes confusing charges using reasoning paths retrieved from similar cases ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . (4) Post-Training Methods: Vanilla SFT fine-tunes the model on selected successful trajectories. Standard GRPO optimizes the policy using trajectory-level outcome rewards. SmartSearch uses general principles to optimize search queries.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 presents the main experimental results. LegalEvolver achieves the best overall performance on both datasets and outperforms all baselines. We further make the following observations. (1) Agentic retrieval generally improves legal judgment prediction over direct reasoning. External retrieval provides fine-grained legal knowledge that may not be reliably available in the model’s parametric knowledge, thereby grounding legal qualification and sentencing decisions in relevant evidence. (2) LegalEvolver consistently outperforms existing search agents through rubric-guided policy optimization. Our rubrics guide the policy to formulate queries around unresolved legal uncertainties, enabling it to retrieve more useful evidence than retrieval access alone. In contrast, existing agents largely rely on general query optimization and often formulate overly coarse queries that omit latent legal issues and legally salient case details. (3) Rubric–policy co-evolution provides stronger alignment than one-stage post-training. LegalEvolver combines outcome supervision with query-level feedback and refreshes the rubric bank using trajectories from the updated policy. The resulting improvements across all three prediction tasks indicate that iterative supervision remains aligned with the policy as its search behavior evolves. We provide controlled ablations of the key components in Appendix F .

paragraphs.en: To assess the effectiveness of query-level supervision and iterative rubric refinement, Figure 2 compares LegalEvolver with Standard GRPO and Fixed Rubric GRPO on CAIL2018 and CMDL across three training rounds. All methods start from the same SFT checkpoint and use the same total number of optimization steps. Each checkpoint reports the mean accuracy over law article, charge, and prison-term prediction. Two observations validate our design. (1) Legal query supervision improves reward alignment. LegalEvolver converges faster and consistently outperforms Standard GRPO, which relies only on trajectory-level outcome feedback. The steeper learning curves suggest that rewarding queries that translate case facts into targeted legal questions about specific legal uncertainties provides more effective supervision than outcome feedback alone. (2) Rubric–policy co-evolution sustains improvement across training rounds. Fixed Rubric GRPO uses the initial rubric bank throughout all three rounds and shows diminishing gains in later training, whereas LegalEvolver continues to improve by refining the rubric bank with trajectories generated by the updated policy. This controlled comparison rules out additional training steps as the source of improvement and shows that iterative rubric refinement keeps query supervision aligned with the policy’s evolving search behavior.

paragraphs.en: We analyze the erroneous trajectories produced by all methods and summarize their dominant query failure patterns in Figure 3 (a). We define a trajectory as erroneous when either its charge or law article prediction is incorrect, and use GLM-5.2 ( GLM-5-Team et al., 2026 ) to assign each erroneous trajectory to an error category. The dominant failure patterns can be grouped into three broad categories: repeated searches based on incorrect assumptions, omission of key case facts, and under-specified retrieval intent. LegalEvolver produces the fewest erroneous trajectories, with fewer repetitive and coarse-grained queries. This pattern is consistent with our training strategy, which encourages the policy to formulate queries that directly address specific legal uncertainties and retrieve the evidence needed to resolve them.
paragraphs.zh: 我们分析了所有方法产生的错误轨迹，并在图 3 (a) 中总结了其主要查询失败模式。 当轨迹的电荷或法条预测错误时，我们将其定义为错误轨迹，并使用 GLM-5.2（GLM-5-Team et al., 2026）将每条错误轨迹归入一个错误类别。 主要失败模式可归纳为三大类：基于错误假设的重复搜索、遗漏关键案件事实，以及检索意图不明确。 LegalEvolver 产生的错误轨迹最少，重复查询和粗粒度查询也更少。 这一模式与我们的训练策略一致，该策略鼓励智能体制定能够直接针对特定法律不确定性并检索所需证据以解决这些不确定性的查询。

paragraphs.en: To assess whether LegalEvolver addresses these failures, we evaluate query quality along four dimensions: Legal Specificity , whether queries contain case-specific legal concepts and key facts; Legal-Issue Completeness , whether the query set covers the main legal issues required for a complete judgment; Retrieval Actionability , whether queries are clearly formulated and can directly guide the selected tool to retrieve useful evidence; and Alternative Awareness , whether queries consider plausible competing legal interpretations and seek the evidence needed to distinguish among them, rather than only supporting an initial hypothesis. We use three independent LLM judges to score anonymized query sets from all methods on 300 cases from each dataset. As shown in Figure 3 (b), LegalEvolver ranks first on all four dimensions and achieves the highest overall score. Its advantages in Legal Specificity and Alternative Awareness show that the learned policy more effectively translates case facts into targeted legal questions and explores competing interpretations before reaching a judgment. In contrast, general-purpose query optimization does not fully address the task-specific information needs of legal judgment prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 为评估 LegalEvolver 是否解决了这些缺陷，我们从四个维度评估查询质量：法律具体性，即查询是否包含针对案件的法律概念和关键事实；法律争点完整性，即查询集合是否覆盖作出完整判断所需的主要法律争点；检索可操作性，即查询是否表述清晰、能否直接引导所选工具检索有用证据；以及替代方案意识，即查询是否考虑合理的竞争性法律解释并寻求区分它们所需的证据，而不仅仅是支持一个初始假设。 我们使用三个独立的 LLM 评审者，对来自每个数据集 300 个案件的所有方法的匿名查询集合进行打分。 如图 3 (b) 所示，LegalEvolver 在所有四个维度上排名第一，并取得了最高的总体得分。 它在法律具体性和替代方案意识上的优势表明，所学到的策略能更有效地将案件事实转化为有针对性的法律问题，并在作出判断前探索竞争性的解释。 相比之下，通用的查询优化并未能完全满足法律判决预测这一任务特定的信息需求。

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 takes the tool statute_search as an example to illustrate how the rubric bank evolves across training stages. For legal qualification, the rubrics progress from isolated legal concepts and case details to reusable factual dimensions and explicit criteria for identifying offense boundaries and distinguishing potentially applicable charges. For sentencing, they evolve from simple amount-related cues to structured coverage of the conduct, object, outcome, amount, frequency, and timing that determine statutory sentencing tiers. These examples show how rubric–policy co-evolution turns local retrieval heuristics revealed by updated trajectories into more comprehensive and reusable query supervision, enabling the policy to formulate searches that better address the legal uncertainty at each reasoning stage.
paragraphs.zh: 图 4 以工具 statute_search 为例，说明题库在训练各阶段中如何演进。 在法律定性方面，评分标准从孤立的法律概念和案件细节，逐步发展为可复用的事实维度，以及用于识别罪名边界和区分潜在适用罪名的明确标准。 在量刑方面，评分标准从简单的数额相关线索，演进为对决定法定量刑档次的行为、对象、结果、数额、频次和时间等要素的结构化覆盖。 这些示例展示了评分标准与策略的协同演化如何将更新轨迹所揭示的局部检索启发式，转化为更全面且可复用的查询监督，使策略能够制定更能应对各推理阶段法律不确定性的检索。

paragraphs.en: We presented LegalEvolver , a framework that improves legal judgment prediction by explicitly optimizing the retrieval queries generated during agent reasoning. LegalEvolver induces rubrics from within-case trajectory contrasts and uses them to supervise intermediate queries during policy optimization. It then refines the rubric bank using trajectories generated by the updated policy, enabling the policy and the rubrics to co-evolve through alternating updates. Experimental results show that LegalEvolver achieves the strongest overall performance and produces more legally specific and informative queries that better address unresolved legal uncertainties. Further analyses indicate that the evolving rubrics remain aligned with changes in the policy’s search behavior, enabling continued improvement beyond one-stage post-training. These findings demonstrate the value of rubric–policy co-evolution for evidence-grounded legal judgment prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 LegalEvolver，一个通过显式优化智能体推理过程中生成的检索查询来改进法律判决预测的框架。 LegalEvolver 从个案内轨迹对比中归纳评分标准（rubrics），并在策略优化过程中用它们来监督中间查询。 随后，它利用更新后的策略生成的轨迹来精炼评分标准库，使策略与评分标准能够通过交替更新实现共同进化。 实验结果表明，LegalEvolver 取得了最强的整体性能，并生成更具法律针对性和信息量的查询，能够更好地应对未解决的法律不确定性。 进一步分析表明，不断进化的评分标准始终与策略搜索行为的变化保持一致，从而在单阶段后训练之外实现持续改进。 这些发现证明了评分标准—策略共同进化对于基于证据的法律判决预测的价值。

paragraphs.en: This work studies legal judgment prediction using the publicly available CAIL2018 and CMDL research datasets together with public legal materials, including statutes, judicial interpretations, sentencing guidelines, and precedents. We do not collect new personal data or attempt to identify individuals, and we report results in aggregate without reproducing identifying case details. Nevertheless, criminal cases may contain sensitive facts, and automated legal predictions can inherit errors and social biases from the underlying data, retrieval corpora, and language models. The resulting system is intended solely for research and should not be used as legal advice or as a substitute for qualified legal professionals and judicial decision-makers. Any practical deployment would require jurisdiction-specific validation, appropriate privacy safeguards, careful bias assessment, and meaningful human oversight.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究使用公开可获取的 CAIL2018 和 CMDL 研究数据集以及公开法律材料（包括法律法规、司法解释、量刑指南和判例）来研究法律判决预测。 我们不收集新的个人数据，也不试图识别个人身份，并且我们以汇总形式报告结果，不复现可识别身份的案件细节。 尽管如此，刑事案件可能包含敏感事实，而且自动化法律预测可能会从底层数据、检索语料库和语言模型中继承错误与社会偏见。 所得到的系统仅用于研究目的，不应被用作法律建议，也不应替代合格的法律专业人员和司法决策者。 任何实际部署都需要进行针对特定司法管辖区的验证、适当的隐私保护、审慎的偏见评估以及有意义的人工监督。

paragraphs.en: Reinforcement learning has advanced tool-augmented reasoning through self-taught tool use in START ( Li et al., 2025a ) and reward-driven tool learning in ToolRL ( Qian et al., 2025 ) . ReSearch applies RL to interleaved reasoning and search ( Chen et al., 2025 ) . However, outcome-only rewards provide sparse feedback for intermediate search decisions, motivating step-wise supervision ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . In the legal domain, MSR 2 targets sentencing-factor identification ( Chen et al., 2026 ) , while SyLeR uses structure-aware rewards to encourage syllogistic reasoning ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) . In general-purpose search, SmartSearch evaluates query novelty, intent necessity, and retrieval relevance ( Wen et al., 2026 ) , while StepSearch uses information gain and redundancy penalties for step-wise RL ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . These methods motivate our complementary focus on intermediate query construction and legally grounded search feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 强化学习通过START（Li et al., 2025a）中的自学习工具使用以及ToolRL（Qian et al., 2025）中奖励驱动的工具学习，推动了工具增强推理的发展。 ReSearch将强化学习应用于推理与搜索的交错进行（Chen et al., 2025）。 然而，仅基于结果的奖励为中间搜索决策提供的反馈十分稀疏，这促使研究者引入逐步监督（Zheng et al., 2025）。 在法律领域，MSR 2针对量刑要素识别（Chen et al., 2026），而SyLeR则利用结构感知奖励来鼓励三段论式推理（Zhang et al., 2025）。 在通用搜索方面，SmartSearch评估查询的新颖性、意图必要性与检索相关性（Wen et al., 2026），而StepSearch则利用信息增益和冗余惩罚进行逐步强化学习（Zheng et al., 2025）。 这些方法促使我们将研究重点放在互补的中间查询构建以及基于法律的搜索反馈上。

paragraphs.en: Beyond its application to legal retrieval, LegalEvolver makes two methodological advances. (1) Compared with existing legal search agents, it converts within-case contrasts between successful and failed trajectories into explicit supervision for intermediate query construction. The resulting rubrics directly reward whether a query addresses the unresolved legal issue, rather than relying only on final judgment accuracy or general reasoning structure. (2) Compared with general-domain evolving-rubric methods such as DR Tulu ( Shao et al., 2025 ) , LegalEvolver conditions the rubric bank on both retrieval tool and reasoning focus, so different knowledge sources and reasoning stages receive distinct criteria. The bank is then updated from the improved policy’s trajectories and filtered through held-out revalidation, coupling rubric evolution to fine-grained retrieval decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 除了在法律检索中的应用外，LegalEvolver 还带来了两项方法学进展。 （1）与现有的法律搜索智能体相比，它将同一案件中成功轨迹与失败轨迹之间的对比转化为对中间查询构建的显式监督。 由此得到的评分标准直接衡量查询是否解决了未决的法律问题，而不是仅仅依赖最终判决的准确性或一般的推理结构。 （2）与 DR Tulu（Shao et al., 2025）等通用领域的演进式评分标准方法相比，LegalEvolver 将评分标准库同时以检索工具和推理焦点为条件，从而使不同的知识来源和推理阶段获得各自不同的评判标准。 随后，评分标准库根据改进后策略的轨迹进行更新，并通过留出集再验证进行筛选，将评分标准的演进与细粒度的检索决策耦合起来。

paragraphs.en: Legal judgment prediction requires dedicated reasoning over fine-grained legal knowledge, rather than relying solely on the knowledge stored in model parameters. To support agentic legal reasoning with reliable external evidence, we construct a multi-source legal knowledge environment consisting of law articles, precedents, judicial interpretations, and sentencing guidelines, together with their corresponding retrieval tools. These four knowledge sources provide complementary evidence from different perspectives, namely statutory constituent elements, judicial experience, rules for legal application, and sentencing standards, thereby supporting article prediction, charge prediction, and sentence prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 法律判决预测需要对细粒度法律知识进行专门的推理，而不能仅依赖模型参数中存储的知识。 为了支持基于可靠外部证据的智能体法律推理，我们构建了一个多来源法律知识环境，包含法律条文、判例、司法解释和量刑指南，以及与之对应的检索工具。 这四类知识来源从不同视角提供互补证据，即法定构成要件、司法经验、法律适用规则和量刑标准，从而支持法条预测、罪名预测和刑期预测。

Each entry combines the article number with its statutory text as the dense-search representation. paragraphs.en: Across all four tools, we encode retrieval text with the 768-dimensional SAILER-zh encoder ( Li et al., 2023 ) , L2-normalize the embeddings, and use exact FAISS inner-product search. paragraphs.en: We construct SFT and GRPO data from the training portions of CAIL2018 and CMDL. During SFT data construction, each complete agent trajectory is decomposed into step-level examples for first-step planning from the case facts, next-action prediction under tool observations, and final legal-judgment prediction. This procedure yields 19,111 step-level SFT examples. The GRPO training set contains 1,448 cases drawn from the two datasets. For each GRPO round, we repeatedly sample with the model obtained from the preceding training round and retain cases that remain difficult across multiple attempts.
paragraphs.zh: 我们基于 CAIL2018 和 CMDL 的训练部分构建 SFT 与 GRPO 数据。 在构建 SFT 数据时，每条完整的智能体轨迹被分解为步骤级样本，涵盖基于案件事实的首步规划、工具观测下的下一动作预测，以及最终的法律判决预测。 该流程共生成 19,111 条步骤级 SFT 样本。 GRPO 训练集包含取自这两个数据集的 1,448 个案件。 在每一轮 GRPO 中，我们使用上一轮训练得到的模型反复采样，并保留在多次尝试中仍然困难的案件。

sents.en: All GRPO-based variants use the same training data, optimization steps, and training configuration as LegalEvolver. w/o rubric evolution keeps the initial rubric bank fixed and does not update it using trajectories generated by the improved policy. w/o rubric rewards retains only the outcome and format rewards. w/o targeted rubrics replaces the rubric bank organized by retrieval tool and reasoning focus with a single shared rubric for all queries. w/o GRPO removes reinforcement learning, whereas w/o SFT uses the base model without subsequent post-training.
sents.zh: 所有基于 GRPO 的变体均使用与 LegalEvolver 相同的训练数据、优化步骤和训练配置。w/o rubric evolution 保持初始评分标准库固定不变，不使用改进策略生成的轨迹对其进行更新。w/o rubric rewards 仅保留结果奖励和格式奖励。w/o targeted rubrics 将按检索工具和推理重点组织的评分标准库替换为对所有查询共享的单一评分标准。w/o GRPO 移除了强化学习，而 w/o SFT 则使用未经后续后训练的基础模型。

paragraphs.en: LegalEvolver achieves the best prediction performance across all metrics. We make three observations. (1) Continual rubric evolution improves the policy. Keeping the initial rubric bank fixed consistently reduces performance, showing that updating the rubrics with trajectories from the improved policy allows the supervision to adapt to changes in its search behavior and provide further gains. (2) Rubric rewards, rather than additional optimization steps, drive the improvement. Without rubric rewards, outcome-only GRPO is trained on the same data for the same total number of steps, yet it still falls clearly behind LegalEvolver. This controlled comparison rules out extra training steps as the source of the gain and demonstrates the value of direct query-level supervision. (3) Rubric specialization is important. A single generic rubric provides limited improvement, whereas organizing the rubric bank by retrieval tool and reasoning focus yields consistently better performance. This result indicates that effective query criteria depend on both the knowledge source being searched and the legal issue being resolved.
paragraphs.zh: LegalEvolver 在所有指标上均取得了最佳的预测性能。 我们得出三点观察。 (1) 持续的评分标准演进能够改进策略。 保持初始评分标准库固定不变会持续降低性能，这表明利用改进后策略产生的轨迹来更新评分标准，能够使监督适应其搜索行为的变化并带来进一步的收益。 (2) 推动改进的是评分标准奖励，而非额外的优化步骤。 在没有评分标准奖励的情况下，仅基于结果的 GRPO 在相同数据上以相同的总步数进行训练，但仍然明显落后于 LegalEvolver。 这一受控比较排除了额外训练步骤作为收益来源的可能性，并证明了直接查询级监督的价值。 (3) 评分标准的专门化非常重要。 单一的通用评分标准只能带来有限的改进，而按检索工具和推理重点来组织评分标准库则始终能带来更好的性能。 这一结果表明，有效的查询标准既取决于所搜索的知识来源，也取决于所解决的法律问题。
